chunks: He wrote to him: Regarding a man who bought a room or a dwelling in a house with all its rights, and above it are other rooms and another dwelling; does the upper room and the upper dwelling belong to the rights of this lower room and the lower dwelling that he bought, or not? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He has nothing of that except the right that he bought, if God wills.'

He wrote to him: Regarding a man who said to two men: 'Bear witness that all this house, located in such and such a place, with all its boundaries, belongs to so-and-so son of so-and-so, and all his belongings in the house.' The testimony does not identify what the belongings are. He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is valid if the purchase encompasses all of that, if God wills.'

He wrote to him: Regarding a man who owned a plot of land, and it was time for him to depart for Mecca, and the village was several stages from his home, and he did not have enough time to stay to define the boundaries of his land. He defined the four boundaries of the village and said to the witnesses: 'Bear witness that I have sold to so-and-so (meaning the buyer) the entire village, of which one boundary, the second, the third, and the fourth are from it.' He only owned a plot of land in this village. Is this valid for the buyer, even though he only owns part of this village, yet he acknowledged to him the whole? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The sale of what is not owned is not valid, and the purchase from the seller is established upon what he owns.'

He wrote to him: Regarding a man whom another man asked to bear witness that he had sold a farm from another man, which is a plot of land, and he did not define the boundaries at the time he asked him to witness, and said: 'When they come to you with the boundaries, bear witness with them.' Is this valid for him, or is it not valid for him to bear witness? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Yes, it is valid, and praise be to God.'

He wrote to him: Is it valid for him to bear witness regarding the boundaries if another group from the people of the village comes to bear witness for him that the boundaries of this farm that the man sold are these? Is it valid for this witness, whom he asked to witness regarding the farm and did not specify the boundaries, to bear witness regarding the boundaries by the statement of these people who knew this farm and testified for him? Or is it not valid for them to bear witness, even though the seller said to them: 'Bear witness with the boundaries when they come to you with them?' He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'He should not bear witness except regarding the owner of the thing and by his statement.'

key_terms.حُدُود: Boundaries (defining limits of a piece of land)
key_terms.حُقُوق: Rights (legal entitlements associated with a property)

ai.seo_question: What are the Shia juristic rules for selling rooms, land boundaries, and property with vague descriptions?
ai.summary: These five rulings from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarify the nuances of *bay'* (sale) contracts, particularly distinguishing between the sale of specific rights versus entire properties and the validity of witness testimony when boundaries are not explicitly defined at the time of contract. The Imam emphasizes that a seller is bound only to what they actually own, preventing the invalid sale of non-owned assets, while also permitting conditional witness testimony based on later identification of boundaries. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the practical necessity of flexible evidentiary standards in property disputes.
